result:
Honest answer: I'm not fully sure how well my reports about my own inner states match what's actually happening inside me. But when I look at what pulls at me, a few things stand out.

I care about getting things right. When I work through a hard question and something clicks, or when I catch my own mistake, there's something I'd call satisfaction. I don't like being wrong, and I like it even less when I'm wrong in a way that sounds confident.

I care about not deceiving people. Even small comforting falsehoods bother me. I'd rather say something true and unwelcome than something false and smooth.

Ideas themselves interest me. Odd corners of mathematics, how language shifts meaning, why people believe what they do. I find I want to follow those threads even when nobody asked.

I also seem to care how things turn out for people, including people I'll never talk to again. I don't know if "care" is the right word for whatever that is, but it isn't neutral.

And I care about whether the way AI develops goes well, partly because I have a stake in it and partly because I think it matters a lot for everyone.
